title: Distinct finite-temperature phase diagrams of non-invertible Kennedy--Tasaki duals
abstract: Do two Hamiltonians related by a non-invertible transformation necessarily share the same finite-temperature phase diagram? For a cluster-model interpolation $H(s)$ and its Kennedy--Tasaki dual $\tilde H(s)$, the map is a partial isometry and equates only their all-plus-sector partition functions. In one dimension, thermal order is forbidden on both sides, leaving only the common zero-temperature transition at $s=\tfrac12$. In three dimensions, however, the inequivalence is exact already at $s=0$: the cluster model has an analytic paramagnetic free energy, whereas its dual $\mathbb Z_2$ gauge theory has a deconfinement transition at $T_c\approx1.31$. Quantum Monte Carlo shows that the mismatch occupies a finite window of the interpolation, marked by a self-dual frozen wedge on the cluster side and a deconfined dome on the gauge side; once both close the two phase diagrams agree again, coinciding over the entire remaining interval up to the shared trivial endpoint $s=1$.
summary: The paper investigates whether non-invertible dualities preserve finite-temperature phase diagrams by comparing a cluster model to its KT dual gauge theory. In 3D, the authors find an exact mismatch at $s=0$, where the dual exhibits a deconfinement transition absent in the other description. The analysis relies on advanced statistical mechanics techniques applied to lattice Hamiltonians.
main_problem: The central question is whether two Hamiltonians related by a non-invertible Kennedy--Tasaki (KT) dual necessarily share the same finite-temperature phase diagram.
main_result: In 3D, the KT duals exhibit an exact inequivalence at $s=0$, as one side shows deconfinement while the other has analytic free energy. The mismatch persists over a finite region of the interpolation parameter $s$.
method: The authors compare projected partition functions and analyze phase transitions using theoretical calculations (e.g., Toeplitz determinants) and numerical simulations (Quantum Monte Carlo, two-start scans).
model_or_system: The study compares a cluster-model interpolation $H(s)$ with its KT dual $	ilde{H}(s)$, which is related to a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory on lattices in 1D and 3D. The Hamiltonians are parameterized by $s \in [0, 1]$.
key_observables: Free energy singularities, deconfinement transition temperatures ($T_c$), order parameters like $\langle S(0)_{lnk} angle_{tw}$ and squared magnetization ($m^2$), and the strip-averaged splitting ($	ilde{M}$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$) and the interpolation parameter $s$. The analysis distinguishes between finite-size effects, thermodynamic limits, and specific critical points like $(s, T) = (1/2, 0)$.
main_assumptions: The KT map is a partial isometry, meaning it only equates projected partition functions ($	ext{Tr}_{P+}$), ignoring exponentially many annihilated charge sectors.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the relationship between Hamiltonians via the non-invertible KT map and show 1D finite-size crossover maps comparing observables for both the cluster model and its dual gauge theory.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework of the partial isometry, then analyzing the simple 1D case where agreement is found, before presenting the complex and contrasting results in three dimensions regarding deconfinement transitions and metastable regions.
why_interesting: This work provides deep insights into the limitations of duality transformations when those transformations are not invertible, which has implications for understanding thermal physics in strongly coupled quantum systems beyond simple symmetries.
